title: Projects Host & Project Studio
summary: The shared NAS platform that serves the tools, checks access, preserves saved drafts and publishes reviewed releases. Project Studio provides a workflow for creating a work copy, requesting a change and reviewing it before publishing. Access Manager controls which projects a person can open; source backup, publishing and saved-data backup are separate operations.
features: Search/filter tools, read previews and open dedicated project pages.
Owner-managed per-project grants behind authenticated sign-in.
Create a separate work copy, request changes and review before publishing.
Persist shared app designs on the NAS independently of the Windows PC.
Curate files, validate, sign, deploy and verify a release with rollback on failed startup.
Owner-only version history and deliberate restoration workflow.
Gateway routes to HA, CAD, plant, QR backup and other protected services.
workflows: Use search or category filters in the project library. Open Preview to see what a tool does; Open tool goes to the actual application.
Only projects granted to the signed-in account are shown. An owner-only tool is not shared by simply copying its URL.
Use the project’s own save status and export options; the library overview itself does not save its designs.
Review a change in Project Studio
Choose the intended project and create a work copy. Describe the change with a concrete example of the desired behaviour.
Inspect the changed files and test the affected workflow in that work copy. Keep unrelated tools and live saved data outside the change.
Publish only after review/checks finish, then verify the actual hosted version and essential actions. A successful local edit is not a live deployment.
Open Access Manager as the owner, enter the intended person’s email and choose only the requested projects.
Save the grants and share the normal sign-in link. Confirm access as appropriate without weakening the server checks.
Revoke unwanted grants through the same owner workflow. LAN access is not an exception to authentication and authorisation.
Before editing a shared saved design, read its live API version/ETag and preserve newer changes. Do not restore a source seed over a live draft.
For application updates, use the signed release workflow and inspect verification output. Keep deployment keys out of Git.
Use version restore as an explicit owner operation after identifying the target version. Back up live data separately; a Git commit is not a copy of the database or uploads.
limits: This is installation-specific infrastructure and remains private. A portable public edition needs a configuration/authentication guide and clean deployment testing. The demo changes only mock permissions, work copies and release state.
